name: Nitroimidazoles
summary: Antibiotic and antiparasitic medicines, including metronidazole and tinidazole, that act on susceptible bacteria and parasites that live without oxygen.
mechanism: Nitroimidazoles are switched on inside susceptible organisms by pathways that are absent in aerobic human cells. The switched-on form produces short-lived products that bind to DNA and damage it. In Giardia, enzymes such as pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase help to switch on 5-nitroimidazoles including metronidazole and tinidazole.
cautions: For metronidazole, the NHS advises avoiding alcohol during treatment and for 2 days afterwards.
Tinidazole is described as similar to metronidazole in its range of activity and side effects, so similar cautions may apply.
classEffects: Feeling sick, diarrhoea and a metallic taste are the common side effects of metronidazole.

references.title: PubMed: Mode of action of metronidazole on anaerobic bacteria and protozoa
